chronology: [Prior volume recap] Shabda-Oud Mother Superior arrives on Okhar in a Cetacyborg with two assassins; interrogates Honorata, who lies that her child is hermaphroditic
Aghnar defeats the assassins using epyphite-tipped prosthetics; Honorata links her power to his in a telepathic duel against the Mother Superior
Othon infiltrates and destroys the Cetacyborg from inside using viral tactics, but is fatally contaminated by its toxic gases in the process
Honorata reveals she carries a micro-H bomb wired to her artificial heart and cannot safely leave; Othon and Aghnar depart in the Metabunker
Honorata and Okhar are annihilated from orbit; Othon and Aghnar vow revenge
Metabunker lands on Planet Perdita (lower system), half-submerged in a muddy lake under the planet's extreme gravity
Othon tells Aghnar he has dispatched spy-needles across the universe; signals will not return for ten years; they must remain hidden on Perdita in the meantime
Othon reveals he is dying from Cetacyborg gas contamination; his blood is poisoned and he has only days left
Othon demands Aghnar kill him, framing it as the Castaka initiation rite and the proof of strength needed to one day destroy the Shabda-Oud army
Father and son duel in the Metabunker; Aghnar uses psychic eye-beam powers but is left paralyzed; Othon warns he has Oko mini-bombs distributed throughout his body
Aghnar shoots Othon in the head, completing the Castaka patricide rite
Aghnar enters roughly ten years of isolation on Perdita, tended only by robots including Lothar and Tonto, awaiting the spy-needle signals
Aghnar preserves Othon's corpse in deep-freeze, then performs a prolonged surgical operation to extract the Oko mini-bombs from the body and graft them into his own
Aghnar ventures outside on Perdita; using an epyphite-soaked dart he captures a falling ape-like creature and brings it home
Aghnar heals the wounded ape with synthesized green blood; the creature proves rational and capable of speech; Aghnar names it before it leaps away once restored
Aghnar and the ape companion ascend above a mushroom-dome settlement, entering territory of an alien tribal society ruled by a combat-dominant Patriarch
Aghnar fights through swarms of alien tribe creatures, fulfilling the Magon prophecy of a 'little white ape' who will lead them away
On Aghnar's eighteenth birthday, while a wounded ape-like figure is being treated, a long-awaited spy-needle signal arrives
Aghnar learns the Shabda-Oud comet is guarded by six cetacyborgs; a seventh is on a covert mission to the blue solar system of Beta-Kuntri

Aghnar loads Magon apes into the Metabunker with a false promise of passage to the Diamond Planet; the apes are rendered comatose by heat-immunizing injection and jettisoned as organic feed to lure the seventh cetacyborg
Aghnar infiltrates the seventh cetacyborg alone in an armored space suit, working through its exterior hull into its internal machinery passages
Inside, Aghnar ambushes the Shabda-Oud sisters, shoots one, and uses mental coercion to force the others to reveal the secret destination of their voyage
Aghnar learns the sisters are traveling to Baggadathi; Shabda-Oud superiors believe Oda Capricious united with Aghnar's bloodline will produce a supreme being capable of dethroning Janus-Jana
Aghnar views a holovid of Oda Capricious and becomes intensely captivated; he concludes seduction is necessary because her pride makes abduction impossible
Oda's marriage condition is a blue rose, said to have been extinct for thirty thousand years
Cetacyborg finishes feeding and becomes responsive; Aghnar orders crew to stay back, takes a small moto-craft toward Amadis on Baggadathi — to be continued
locations: Planet Perdita (lower system): small granite-and-mud world shrouded in fog; extreme gravity; hosts 160-foot mushrooms, floating apes, and flat voracious ground creatures; Metabunker is half-submerged in a muddy lake here
Metabunker: the Castaka family's mobile fortress and vessel; contains armories, surgical bays, deep-freeze storage, and living quarters
Okhar (destroyed): Honorata's home planet, annihilated by the micro-H bomb in the opening recap
Shabda-Oud comet: ice asteroid transformed into a comet; the Shabda-Oud's base, currently guarded by six cetacyborgs
Blue solar system of Beta-Kuntri: destination of the Shabda-Oud's seventh cetacyborg on its covert mission
Magon territory: a landscape of clustered mushroom domes inhabited by an alien tribal proto-civilization with a Patriarch hierarchy; the sky above contains a vast luminous swirling formation
Baggadathi (Septennial system): described as the richest planet in the system; home of the royal city Amahdis and of Oda Capricious
Amadis / Amahdis: royal city on Baggadathi; birthplace of Oda; Aghnar's destination at the volume's end
Diamond Planet: a promised or mythic destination invoked in Magon prophecy and used as a false lure for the apes; exact location unconfirmed
lore_laws: Castaka tradition requires a Metabaron to kill his own father as the qualifying initiation act

Cetacyborgs are gigantic semi-organic vessels used by the Shabda-Oud as guardians and transports; they can be destroyed from within by viral infiltration but the infiltrator is fatally contaminated by the vessel's toxic gases
Epyphite-tipped prosthetics and darts are effective against Shabda-Oud assassins

Oko mini-bombs are implantable devices that detonate if the host body is pierced; they are distributed throughout the body rather than placed in the brain, and can be surgically extracted and re-implanted in a new host
Mental or psychic powers can be used offensively as visible projected energy; they can substitute for physical combat but do not prevent paralysis
The Shabda-Oud inhabit an ice asteroid transformed into a comet; six cetacyborgs guard it at any given time, with a reported fleet total of seven
Spy-needles are small vessels capable of long-range travel and communication; signals take approximately ten years to return across the universe
Synthesized green blood can be used to save beings with severe organic trauma
The Magon tribal Patriarch holds dominance through combat, contested on a recurring ritual occasion; the Patriarch is said to live roughly thirty thousand years
A cetacyborg responds to neurological control commands but its primal feeding instinct can override those commands
Blue roses are said to have been extinct for thirty thousand years
major_events: Honorata's death and Okhar's destruction (recap): the bomb in Honorata's artificial heart annihilates both her and the planet; Othon and Aghnar vow revenge from orbit
Othon's ritual death: dying from Cetacyborg gas contamination, Othon forces Aghnar into a lethal duel and demands patricide as Castaka initiation; Aghnar kills him
Aghnar's ten-year isolation on Planet Perdita: alone with robots, he preserves Othon's corpse, surgically grafts Oko mini-bombs into himself, and masters the hostile environment
Aghnar befriends and names a rational ape-like creature, forging a bond that becomes the foundation for his relationship with the Magon proto-civilization
Aghnar fulfills the Magon prophecy by defeating the tribal Patriarch and earning leadership as the 'little white ape' figure
Arrival of the spy-needle signal on Aghnar's eighteenth birthday marks the end of the isolation period and triggers the active revenge campaign
Trojan-horse operation: Magon apes sacrificed as cetacyborg feed; Aghnar infiltrates the vessel solo and mentally subdues the Shabda-Oud sisters inside
Aghnar learns of Oda Capricious and the bloodline prophecy; sets course for Baggadathi resolved to win her, ending the volume on an open pursuit
open_uncertainties: The silver-haired youth called Kiowotai (p12-13) and the figure called Kioka (p17) may be Aghnar as perceived by the Magon, or may be a separate named character; the relationship is not resolved on these pages
Whether Diaghana — who sought kingship over the apes and disrupted their ecology — is a character distinct from Aghnar or an alias used in the narration is not clarified in this volume
The exact nature of the large luminous swirling formation visible above the mushroom-dome settlement is not identified
Whether the cetacyborg's primal feeding fully severs neurological control or only temporarily disrupts it is unclear
The location and true nature of the Diamond Planet — whether literal, mythic, or deliberate deception — is not established
How Aghnar might fulfill Oda Capricious's blue-rose condition is left entirely open at the volume's close
The full scope of the prophecy linking Oda's union with Aghnar's bloodline to a supreme being capable of dethroning Janus-Jana, and the identity of Janus-Jana, are introduced but not explained
Printed page-footer numbers in several scan images differ from the supplied page labels (notably p15 through p20), creating minor traceability uncertainty
recurring_motifs: Patricide as rite of passage: killing one's father is the required initiation into the Metabaron lineage
Revenge as generational engine: every action Aghnar takes is explicitly tied to avenging Honorata and Okhar
Body modification as self-empowerment: prosthetic limbs, surgically implanted Oko mini-bombs, and grafted enhancements progressively transform Aghnar
Isolation and solitary trial: Aghnar's growth occurs almost entirely without human family or peers
Prophecy fulfilled unknowingly: multiple cultures (Magon, Shabda-Oud) hold legends that Aghnar satisfies without initially seeking them
Deception and infiltration over direct assault: the cetacyborg-as-Trojan-horse mirrors Othon's own lethal infiltration tactic in the prior volume
The impossible gift: Oda's demand for an extinct blue rose echoes other near-unachievable thresholds that define Castaka trials
The Diamond Planet as promised or mythic destination: invoked in Magon prophecy and weaponized as a false lure for the apes
title: The Trials of Aghnar
